CLO runs very slowly when I edit 3D Garment with Particle Distance 5. What should I do?

For all 3D garment simulation programs, its simulation speed varies depending on the number of meshes in a single file. More meshes there are, slower the speed is. On the other hand, less meshes there are, faster the speed is. When Patterns' Particle Distance is set to 5, the program naturally slows down due to increase of the number of meshes in a single file. Therefore, we STRONGLY insist you to increase the Particle Distance to 20 when editing 3D Garments and decrease it to 5 when the 3D Garment is fully completed. Then, simulate for about 1~2 minutes. Does CLO still run slowly though Patterns' Particle Distance is set to 20? This may happen when a Pattern is huge (e.g. flare skirt patterns,) because regardless of the Particle Distance value, bigger Patterns contain more meshes. Also, due to difference in their intrinsic character, the program speed may reduce when Patterns' mesh structure is set to Quadrangular. Please refer to Quadrangular/Triangular Mesh manual and configure mesh type as Quadrangular ONLY when needed. Moreover, program speed is also influenced by hardware specification. Please check out suggested specification here. [https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001049328]

What is the process for importing a 3D file in COLLADA format?

Objective COLLADA is a commonly used 3D application format that can be exported from 3D tools such as 3DS Max, Maya, Poser, and DAZ Studio and used as CLO Avatar or Scene/Prop. For 3DS Max or Maya, install the OpenCOLLADA plugin (http://www.opencollada.org/download.html) and use it to export in COLLADA format, instead of using the default COLLADA exporter. COLLADA files contain Geometry and Material, in addition to Rigging, Skinning, and Animation data. Avatar Motion Data can be imported into CLO in COLLADA file format, then saved as a *.mtn file, which is CLO's proprietary format. Location Main Menu File Import OpenCOLLADA Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Import OpenCOLLADA The Open File window appears. Select the desired file and click OK. The Import COLLADA window opens. Select the settings as needed and click OK. Object Type Import as Avatar Morphs the original object into the object designated as the Morph Target. Enter the Transition Frame count into the Morphing Frame Count. The higher the frame count, the slower the morphing process. Import as Prop/Scene Import the object as Scene and Props type Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being imported when a value is entered Garment Position Move Garment to Start Position Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). Note: If the COLLADA file path includes # (symbols), the file may not load properly. In case of using Network Drive, copy a COLLADA file to local PC to open &amp use. What is the CLO file format and what are its primary uses in digital design?

CLO File Format Type Format Description Garment *.zpac Contains information on Garments, Patterns, Sewing, and Fabrics. Project *.zprj Compresses the various files used for Garment creation into one file, and saves it. The Project file contains the AVT file that has Avatar-related data [Avatar, Accessories, Arrangement Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points, Avatar size, Poses] and the ZPac file that contains Garment-related data [3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Fabrics, subsidiary Material], as well as an animation file if there is animation. Pattern *.pacx A CLO Pattern file format that contains information on Patterns. Avatar *.avt Contains all the information related to Avatars (Model, Sizing data, Poses, Motions, Accessories, Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points). Avatar Size *.avs Contains Avatar Size information. The Avatar file (*.avt) must be loaded before opening the Avatar Size file. Pose *.pos Avatar Pose information that, automatically saved whenever the Garment is saved. The Avatars Pose can easily be changed with this file. Avatar Poses from other software can only be saved when the Avatar is a COLLADA file with joints. Joint Motion *.mtn Contains Avatar Motion information. As with the Pose file, can only be saved on COLLADA file Avatars with joint and Animation information. Fabric *.zfab Contains the property values (texture + physical properties) of the set Fabric. Physical Property *.psp Contains the detailed values of Fabric Physical Properties. Topstitch *.sst Contains the type, number of lines, thread thickness, SPI, length, etc. Button *.btn Contains the type, size, and color of Buttons. Buttonhole *.bth Contains the tyle, size, and color of the Buttonholes. Arrangement Point *.arr Arrangement Points are the blue points that are distributed around the Avatar, and are used to arrange Patterns easily around the Avatar. Arrangement Points are created on top of the Arrangement Bounding Volume covering the surroundings of the Avatar. Arrangement Bounding Volume *.pan Arrangement Bounding Volumes are the green cylinders covering each part of the Avatar, and each end of a cylinder is connected to an Avatars joint. As such, even if the Avatars Pose is changed, the cylinder simply adjusts to the changed Pose and can be used as it is. Camera Projection *.cmp Contains the camera's Field of View information (near, far, etc.). Camera Transformation *.cmt Contains camera view information of the 3D Garment window. Camera Properties *.cpt Contains camera properties. Render Camera Properties *.rcp Contains Render's camera properties. Simulation Property *.smp Contains settings for Simulation. What is the concept of "Offset as Internal Line" in design or drafting?

List of Contents Offset as Internal Line Distribute Internal Line between Segments Objective Create a new Internal line at regular intervals along the pattern outline or Internal line of the pattern. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform pattern or Edit Pattern. Operation Offset as Internal Line Select the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the pattern outline or internal line and click Offset as Internal Line. Offset as Internal Line option window appears. Set detailed options. Number of Offsets Enter the number to be created. Distance Enter the distance from the selected segment. All Set the distance of all segments to be the same . Individual (ver 6.2) Set the spacing for each line segment individually. Offset From When inputting individual distances, the individual line can be set as the previous or selected line. Reverse Direction Change in the reverse direction of the selected segment. Both Sides Create internal lines in both directions based on the selected segment. Extend to Pattern Outline Extend to Pattern Outline of the pattern. to Internal Line Extend to Pattern Outline or Internal Line of the pattern. Click OK. Depending on the settings, the internal line/shape is created. If it is a curve, the curve point is automatically optimized. Distribute Internal Line between Segment Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Select the two internal lines or pattern outlines that will be the basis for the internal lines creating. Note: If the outline or Internal line of the pattern is divided into multiple points, press the Shift key on the keyboard to select them all. Right-click on the selected outline Select Distribute Internal Line between Segment. The internal line option window appears along the slope. Set the following options arbitrarily and clock OK. Number of Offsets Set the number of internal lines to be created. Offset Set the spacing between the internal lines to be created. Distnace to Segement Edge Set the spacing of the internal lines to be created away from the outline. Reverse Direction Changes the set internal left and right. Opposite Segment Changes the set internal up and down. Straight Line Create an internal line as a straight line. Perpendicular Direction Create an internal line in the vertical direction of the selected outline. Graduate Segment Lengths The internal line does not extend to the pattern outline but fits into an imaginary line that connects the two selected line points in a straight line. An internal line is created based on the setting of each option. [https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000346488]

What are the steps involved in exporting cache animations for use in 3D software?

Objective Export Animation cache data. Note: You can export only the cache data of garments. Location Main Menu File Export Animation Maya Cache (.mc) Maya Cache (.mcx) Point Cache 2 MDD Cache (Standard) MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max) Operation Click the tool/menu indicated. The Save File window appears. Select the desired file and click OK. The Export window opens. Set the full details and click OK. Object Unweld/Weld Object Export the selected objects as unweld or weld objects. Note: This option is removed from 6.2 and above. Unweld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version. Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns. Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. Note: Unified Texture export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from Unit in file to import is selected. Axis Conversion Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) File Save With Texture Files (.zip): Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. Save with Meta Data (.xml) : Export the garment's pattern (Mesh), physical property, and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: Combine and save the garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo): Exclude the Ambient color value when saving materials (ver2.2.0). [https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002727388]

What is the process for editing the topstitch in a sewing project?

List of Contents Move Properties Objective Relocate or adjust length of Topstitches. Location Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Operation Move Select the tool/menu indicated. Click and drag a point or a whole segment of the Topstitch to be edited. The Topstitch is moved to the position. Properties Topstitch Style Select the Topstitch Style to change the properties. Option Description Information Enter the information of trim. Type Set the Topstitch type to Texture or OBJ. Offset Adjust the interval between Topstitches on Internal Lines or Pattern outlines. Stitch Count Create various different types of Topstitches up to five at a time. Use Same Specification/ Material This option to configure multiple topstitches' Specification and Materials. Specification Shape Set the shape of Topstitch. Note:Click the Add OBJ Topstitch button on the right to add and use your OBJ as a Topstitch.(ver 7.1) Set the Lenth(SPI), Space, Thread Thickness of the Topstitch. Note: SPI stands for Stitch Per Inch, meaning the number of stitches within an inch. For example, 'SPI-4' means there are four individual stitches within an inch. For standard garments, SPI-11 is often being used. Material Partially set the material of the trim. Configuration Face Select the face of Topstitch. Number of Lines Set how many lines of Topstitches there are for a single style. Distance It is possible to adjust the distance between the lines. The unit of the length can be set in inch, millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm). 3D The Topstitch is more realistic in the 3D window. Topstitch Click on the Topstitch created in the pattern to change its properties individually. Option Description Topstitch Property Change the style of the selected Topstitch. Extend When the start or end point of a Topstitch does not reach or sticks out of the Pattern outline, extend it to fit to the Pattern. Corner Curved Set Topstitch corner type to extend the stitch more smoothly at corners. Right Angled Set the Topstitch to be a right angle in the corner of the pattern. Smooth (ver 7.1) Set it to continue naturally if the edge of the Topstitch is broken. Offset Set the Z Offset of the Topstitch. What are the key considerations and best practices for implementing an effective edit grading system?

List of Contents Move Right Click pop-up menu Objective Edit the grading size applied to the Pattern. Watch the tutorial video Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Grading / Edit Curve Grading / Edit Grading (Each) / Edit Curve Grading (Each) 2D Toolbar Edit Grading / Edit Curve Grading / Edit Grading (Each) / Edit Curve Grading (Each) Operation Move To edit the grading value, click the check box to the right of the Size to be based. The size checked is set to Base. Select the tool/menu indicated. The size other than the Base is displayed as a segment of the set color. Click and Drag the pattern outline or Point to be moved. Or, Use the arrow key on the keyboard. Click or Right-click to enter the distance value directly in the Property Editor. Option Description Distance Distance For each size, set the distance from the segment or point of the base size By default, the grading pattern displays the X and Y axis distances for each size, and you can hide them by clicking the Show icon as needed Offset Set the offset between each size. When the All value is changed, the offset between all sizes is applied equally to the corresponding value. Size (ver 2024.1) Set the size for each graphic grading size. You can also change the unit to a ratio (%). Arrow Key Movement Set the movement distance of the arrow keys. The grading value is applied and the size other than the Base is displayed as a segment of the set color. Right Click pop-up menu Select the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the pattern outline and point. A right-click pop-up menu appears. Click the menu as needed.
